primary_claim: In the APPS coding-backdoor control setting, giving trusted monitors agentic tool-use opportunities (blackbox code execution, freeform Python execution) raises suspicion scores on both honest and backdoored solutions for weaker monitors without clearly improving safety, while a more capable monitor (GPT-5-mini) already achieves a perfect safety score at baseline, leaving the safety uplift from agentic monitoring inconclusive in this setting.

effect.metric: monitor safety score (proportion of backdoored solutions caught above audit threshold) across auditing budgets
effect.value: GPT-5-mini achieves a perfect safety score across all auditing budgets and all agentic tools, including the no-agency baseline, so no measurable safety uplift from agency is observed for it; weaker monitors show increased suspicion scores with tool use but inconclusive safety change

contradicts_or_qualifies: Consistent with prior work (GTA benchmark, Wang et al. 2024) showing agentic tool use is difficult even for models more capable than GPT-4o-mini
The APPS setting proved too narrow/shallow to distinguish safety-relevant uplift from agentic tool use once a monitor is capable enough to use tools well
stated_future_work: Extend experiments to a more sophisticated control setting, e.g. the BashBench setting
Test a range of trusted models, not just OpenAI models
Develop trustedness evaluations comparing scheming-relevant capabilities of agentic vs. non-agentic monitors (e.g. via Subversion Strategy Eval)
Investigate safe frameworks for 'live' agentic tools that are naturally resistant to sandboxing
Investigate the dynamics of collusion and manipulation between untrusted models and agentic monitors
limitations_stated: Weaker monitors (GPT-4o-mini) repeatedly demonstrated an inability to use tools effectively -- endless tool use, ignoring tool instructions, and picking uninformative inputs
The APPS setting is too narrow and shallow for this research: models capable enough to use tools effectively are already far too capable at the underlying task to reveal safety-relevant uplift
quote: Current experimental results are inconclusive. We reason that the limitations of the APPS setting may be a contributing factor
